pull_request.title: Show the VAT breakdown on receipts
pull_request.author: lena-ortiz

gate.reason: No finding was both proven by execution and severe enough to block.

findings.title: invoice_tax_total() sums rounded line taxes, so the total drifts from the rate
findings.body_markdown: Rounding each line before summing (line 41) makes the invoice total differ from `rate * net` by up to one cent per line. Three lines of 333 cents at 19% give 189 where the invoice rate gives 190.

severity.explanation: sensitive path × proven × reachable internally × churn 0.20 × blast radius 0.10

from app.billing.tax import invoice_tax_total


def test_three_lines_total_at_the_invoice_rate():
    assert invoice_tax_total([333, 333, 333], "DE") == 190

findings.title: Take the receipt's currency symbol from the charge, not from the VAT country
findings.body_markdown: `rate_for_country()` now also returns the symbol printed on the receipt (line 29); a Swiss account paying in EUR gets "CHF" beside a euro amount.

findings.title: Annotate the return type of `vat_for()`.
findings.body_markdown: `vat_for()` is the only function in `app/billing/tax.py` without a return annotation.

findings.title: Guard `round_minor()` against two callers running it at once.
findings.body_markdown: Two workers running `round_minor()` together could each overwrite the other's result.

findings.title: Make the invariant in `invoice_tax_total()` explicit.
findings.body_markdown: `invoice_tax_total()` relies on an ordering it never states.
